## Summary

**What** — What changes are introduced in this PR?

Adds a CSV export capability for the customers list, following the existing order and product export patterns. Creates a CustomerExport component and a useExportCustomers hook.

**Why** — Why are these changes relevant or necessary?  

The customers list had no export functionality unlike products and orders which both have export actions. Store managers had no way to extract customer data without direct database access. Closes #17.

**How** — How have these changes been implemented?

- Added useExportCustomers hook to hooks/api/customers.tsx following the useExportOrders pattern
- Created customer-export/customer-export.tsx component modeled on order-export.tsx
- Exported useCustomerTableQuery from hooks/table/query/index.ts (was missing)
- Fixed vite.config.mts React deduplication to resolve blank screen issue

Note: sdk.admin.customer.export() does not currently exist in @medusajs/js-sdk. This PR establishes the UI and hook pattern — full functionality requires the SDK method to be added.

**Testing** — How have these changes been tested, or how can the reviewer test the feature?

Existing tests pass. The hook follows the same pattern as useExportOrders which is already tested.

Summary
The products list has both export and import actions, and the orders list has export, but the customers list has neither. A store manager who wants customer data for a mailing list or a report has no way to get it out of the admin dashboard and has to query the database directly. An export action should be added to the customers list, matching the existing product and order export flows.

User Story
As a store manager, I want to export the customer list to a CSV file, so that I can use customer data in other tools without needing database access.

Rough Scope
Small. The product export and order export flows already exist and can be followed closely, so this is mostly wiring an export action into the customers list and reusing the existing export pattern.

Source
Medusa, admin dashboard customers list page.

## Deliverables

### D1: Sprint Backlog (GitHub Issues)

The team selects and prepares the issues it will implement in Sprint 1.

> **Start this early.** Issues may turn out to be broader than expected, overlap with each other, or be invalid. Discovering this in week 2 leaves no time to recover.

**Step 1: Refine the backlog.** Go through all open issues as a team. Add missing ones, close invalid or duplicate ones, and decompose any large or XL issues into smaller sub-issues that can be completed within the sprint. Record decisions in a team meeting (preferred) or Zulip thread.

**Step 2: Estimate and select.** Use the prioritization and estimation techniques from the planning lecture (story points and planning poker) to size and rank your backlog. Use any units for the story points. Select a set of issues the full team can realistically complete in 2.5 weeks. Your sprint backlog must meet the following minimums:

| Role | Minimum issues selected |
|---|---|
| Each CSCI 435 member | At least 2 medium issues (or equivalent story points) |
| Each CSCI 535 (grad) member | At least 2 medium issues + 1 additional small issue (or equivalent story points) |

> **Quality over quantity.** One well-implemented, thoroughly tested feature is worth more than three half-finished ones. Plan conservatively, then expand if you're ahead of schedule.

> **GitHub Projects.** Consider using GitHub Projects to organize your backlog, track progress, and visualize point burndown. It integrates directly with your issues and milestone. See the GitHub for Beginners tutorial; the Projects section starts at 02:59 in the accompanying video. Try the Team planning or Kanban templates. Team planning supports custom fields such as estimated story points.

**Step 3: Assign ownership.** Every selected issue must have a single owner (assigned in GitHub). One issue per member at minimum; members may own more than one. No issue should be assigned to more than one person.

**Step 4: Create the Sprint 1 milestone.** Create a GitHub Milestone named `Sprint 1` and attach all selected issues to it.

> **Instructor and TA involvement.** The instructor or TA may add new issues or flag specific issues as high priority during the sprint. Treat this as the customer expressing urgency: acknowledge it and adjust your plan accordingly.

> **Suggested pacing.** Aim to have issue specs written and peer-reviewed (see D2) by **Sep 27**. That leaves a bit more than 1.5 weeks for implementation with clear targets in hand. If specs are still being drafted next week, you are likely behind.

**What to provide in D6 (Sprint report):** Link to the Sprint 1 milestone; brief rationale for how you scoped the sprint.

### D2: Requirements Specification

For each issue in your Sprint 1 backlog, the owner must write or significantly refine the specification **before writing any code**.

**Format:** If your project already uses an issue template, adapt it to include the fields below. If your project has no feature request template, create one. Otherwise, use the following structure as a guide.

For **features and enhancements**, write the issue as a user story that satisfies the INVEST criteria (see also the slides on Project management):

```markdown
## User Story
As a [type of user], I want [goal] so that [benefit].

## User Scenario
[A concrete walkthrough of how a user encounters and uses this feature.]

## Acceptance Criteria
1. ...
2. ...
3. ...

## Out of Scope
- ...

## Open Questions
- ...
```

Each acceptance criterion must be **testable**: observable behavior, not vague intent. **Minimum 3 per issue.**

> **What makes a criterion testable?** A testable criterion has a clear pass/fail outcome. "The export button is disabled when no items are selected" is testable. "The UI should feel responsive" is not. If you cannot write a test or manual step that definitively passes or fails it, rewrite it.

For **bug reports**, include at minimum:

```markdown
## Observed Behavior (OB)
[What currently happens.]

## Expected Behavior (EB)
[What should happen instead.]

## Steps to Reproduce (S2R)
1. ...
2. ...

## Additional Information
[Screenshots, stack traces, error logs — recommended.]
```

**Before finalizing your spec,** have at least one teammate read it and leave a comment on the issue confirming it is clear enough to implement. This is a lightweight requirements review.

**Submission:** All issue specs updated in GitHub. Links included in D6.

---

### D3: Design Decisions

For each issue in your Sprint 1 backlog, the owner must document **at least one non-trivial design decision** before or during implementation.

**What to document:**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Decision | One sentence stating what you decided |
| Alternatives considered | At least two concrete options you evaluated |
| Rationale | Why you chose this option over the others |
| Consequences | What this decision makes easier and what it makes harder |

**Where to put it:** Add a `## Design` section to the GitHub issue body, in an issue comment, or include it in the PR description. For decisions that affect multiple issues or the overall architecture, add a team-level note to `docs/sprint1/design.md`.

> **Don't overthink the scope.** "Should I add this field to the existing component or create a new one?" with a clear rationale is a perfectly good design decision. The goal is to make your reasoning visible; one sentence per field is enough. This is not a design document.

**Submission:** Design decisions documented in GitHub issues, PR descriptions, or `docs/sprint1/design.md`. Links in D6.

### D4: Code Changes and Pull Requests

This is the core development activity of Sprint 1. Each team member implements their assigned issue(s) through the full PR workflow.

At least one PR per issue must be created, merged, and closed. In most cases, one issue maps to one PR; if an issue truly requires multiple PRs, split it into sub-issues first.

**Requirements for each PR:**

- Linked to a GitHub issue (`Closes #<number>` in the description).
- Description clearly explains what changed, why, and how it was tested.
- New or updated tests for every behavioral change; test strategy explained in the PR.
- CI should pass if it is configured for your project. If CI is not yet working, document manual verification in the PR description instead. CI setup is encouraged but not required for all projects.
- Reviewed by at least one teammate (not yourself) using the code review rubric below, same process as Sprint 0.
- Merged before the sprint deadline.
- Delete the branch after the PR is merged (same as Sprint 0).

#### Code review rubric

When a PR is ready for review, the reviewer must evaluate it on the criteria below and post the filled-in rubric as a comment on the PR. **Fill in the rubric during your initial review pass, before the author makes any revisions in response to your comments.** Scoring it after all back-and-forth fixes defeats the purpose. If you review a follow-up revision, you may add a brief update to your comment noting what changed.

The Notes column should include a brief explanation (one to two sentences) of your score. Reviewers may also make specific comments on individual lines of code via GitHub's code review interface.

Use this template for your review comment:

```markdown
## Code Review

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Correctness — does the change do what the issue asked? | | |
| Test coverage — are tests present and meaningful? | | |
| Code quality — consistent style, clear naming, no unnecessary duplication | | |
| Documentation — inline comments and PR description are clear | | |
| AI transparency — if AI was used, is there evidence of human verification? | | |
| Overall — would you merge this as-is? | | |
```

Each student must conduct **at least one code review per sprint**. Over the course of the semester, each student must review code from every teammate at least once.

#### Before you write any code

- **Read the issue and spec.** Understand the acceptance criteria before touching any code.
- **Consider using AI.** If you find an agentic tool helpful, use it to validate, extend, or accelerate your understanding, but you must be able to explain every line in your PR.

> **You must be able to explain every line.** Reviewers and the instructor may ask you to explain any part of your change at any time. If you cannot, you will receive points off.

> **Using AI more intentionally.** Before accepting a proposed change, ask the agent to explain what it changed and why, and what could go wrong. This keeps you engaged with the change before it lands in your branch, and gives you something concrete to say during code review.

#### Branch and PR workflow (same as Sprint 0)

For us, replace `main` with `develop` everywhere below.

```bash
# Sync with main before starting
git checkout main
git pull origin main

# Create a branch for your issue
git checkout -b feat/issue-42-export-pdf   # new feature
git checkout -b fix/issue-17-date-overflow  # bug fix

# After making changes and running tests:
git add <changed files>
git commit -m "feat: add PDF export for reports (#42)"
git push origin feat/issue-42-export-pdf
```

After pushing, open the PR via GitHub's "Compare & pull request" banner. Select `main` (`develop` for us) as the base branch.

After your PR is merged, clean up:

```bash
git checkout main           # switch back to main
git pull origin main        # pull the merged changes
git branch -d feat/issue-42-export-pdf  # delete local branch (safe: only works if merged)
```

Also delete the remote branch from GitHub: on the merged PR page, click "Delete branch".

**Submission:** All PRs merged. Links and a summary table in D6.

### D5: AI Logs

Continue the logging practice from Sprint 0. Every agentic session related to Sprint 1 work must be logged. **The requirements below are stricter than Sprint 0.** Review them carefully before submitting.

**Where to store logs:** `ai-logs/sprint1/<your-github-username>/`

**Naming convention:** `YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md`, e.g. `2026-09-25_claude-code_issue-42-pdf-export.md`. Follow the same convention described in AI Log Instructions.

**Format requirements:**

- Logs must capture full session metadata: timestamps, prompts, and AI responses. Use SpecStory or a browser export extension when available (see AI Log Instructions). If no export tool exists for your tool, manually transcribe the session with every message labeled `[User]` or `[AI]` and include timestamps. Do not submit raw, unstructured copy-pastes. Accepted formats: `.md` (preferred), `.txt`, `.json`.
- **Do not summarize or reconstruct your AI usage after the fact.** Logs must be captured during the session.
- **Do not submit `.html`, `.docx`, or `.pdf` log files, or links to private chats.** These will not receive credit.

**Linking:** Reference your log files in a **comment on the corresponding GitHub issue**. Do not add AI log references to the PR description. Use the format and template described in AI Log Instructions. **Logs not linked to an issue comment will not receive credit. Broken links will not receive credit.**

> **Log references go in issue comments only.** Logs may be committed to the repo via a PR, but the reference must still appear in an issue comment, not in the PR description or in a PR comment. Each contributor (implementor, code reviewer, estimator) posts their own comment on the issue. If three people worked on an issue, there should be three separate AI Assistance comments.

If you did not use AI for an issue, post a brief note in an issue comment stating this. No log file is needed for that issue, but your log folder must still exist.

**What to include in D6:** Per member: tools used, number of sessions logged, link to `ai-logs/sprint1/<username>/`, and 2–3 sentences on what worked well or what you'd do differently.

**Submission:** Logs pushed to the repo. Summary in D6.

At the end of Sprint 1, create a release tag to mark the sprint's end state.

- Ensure all Sprint 1 PRs are merged before tagging.
- Use the same base version from Sprint 0 (no version bump).
- Tag with the `-csci435-s1` suffix. Example: if Sprint 0 was `v2.17.2-csci435-s0`, tag Sprint 1 as `v2.17.2-csci435-s1`.
- Write a release description listing features added, bugs fixed, or improvements made this sprint.

```bash
git tag v<version>-csci435-s1
git push origin v<version>-csci435-s1
```

Create the GitHub release from the tag on the repository's Releases page.

**Submission:** Link to the GitHub release in D6. Tag pushed by Oct 8, 11:59 PM.

---

### D8: Reflection Survey (Individual)

Each team member must complete the Sprint 1 reflection survey individually. The link will be distributed via Blackboard and Zulip.

**Deadline:** Oct 8, 11:59 PM.

---

## Grading

Sprint 1 is worth 100 points (10% of the course grade). **D2, D3, D4, D5, and D8 are graded individually; D1, D6, and D7 are graded as a team.**

| Deliverable | Points | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| D1: Sprint Backlog | 10 | Issues selected, estimated, assigned, and attached to milestone; rationale in sprint report |
| D2: Requirements Specification | 20 | Individual. User story format, INVEST criteria, acceptance criteria quality; peer review evidence on issues |
| D3: Design Decisions | 7 | Individual. At least one non-trivial decision documented per issue; rationale is clear |
| D4: Pull Requests | 36 | Individual. Per member: see detail below |
| D5: AI Logs | 7 | Individual. Logs present, correctly formatted, named, and linked to issues; summary in report |
| D6: Sprint Report | 10 | Completeness, specificity, and quality of evidence |
| D7: Sprint Release | 2 | Tag follows convention; description summarizes sprint changes |
| D8: Reflection Survey | 8 | Individual. Required for completion |
| **Total** | **100** | |

### D4 PR grading detail

All PRs associated with each issue are graded on the criteria below. The D4 score is the aggregate across all issues, normalized to 36 points.

| Criterion | Points per PR |
|---|---|
| Change correctly implements the acceptance criteria from D2 | 6 |
| Tests written or updated appropriately; test strategy explained in PR | 5 |
| PR description clearly explains what changed, why, and how it was tested | 4 |
| CI passes (or manual verification documented) | 3 |
| Code reviewed using the rubric; reviewer comment posted on PR | 2 |
| **Total per PR** | **20** |

> **Minimum bar.** A team with no merged PRs (D4), no sprint report (D6), or no release (D7) receives a **0 for Sprint 1** regardless of other deliverables.

> **Extra credit.** A PR submitted to the real upstream project and accepted or under active review earns up to **3 bonus points per PR**, at the instructor's discretion.

- [ ] `docs/sprint1/report.md` (or `.pdf` or `.docx`): sprint report (D6)
- [ ] Sprint 1 release tag pushed and GitHub release created (D7)
- [ ] D8 reflection survey submitted individually by Oct 8, 11:59 PM

import { Button, Heading, toast } from "@medusajs/ui"
import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next"
import { RouteDrawer, useRouteModal } from "../../../components/modals"
import { useExportOrders } from "../../../hooks/api"
import { useOrderTableQuery } from "../../../hooks/table/query"
import { ExportFilters } from "./components/export-filters"

export const OrderExport = () => {
  const { t } = useTranslation()

  return (
    <RouteDrawer>
      <RouteDrawer.Header>
        <RouteDrawer.Title asChild>
          <Heading>{t("orders.export.header")}</Heading>
        </RouteDrawer.Title>
        <RouteDrawer.Description className="sr-only">
          {t("orders.export.description")}
        </RouteDrawer.Description>
      </RouteDrawer.Header>
      <OrderExportContent />
    </RouteDrawer>
  )
}

const OrderExportContent = () => {
  const { t } = useTranslation()
  const { searchParams } = useOrderTableQuery({})

  const { mutateAsync } = useExportOrders(searchParams)
  const { handleSuccess } = useRouteModal()

  const handleExportRequest = async () => {
    await mutateAsync(searchParams, {
      onSuccess: () => {
        toast.info(t("orders.export.success.title"), {
          description: t("orders.export.success.description"),
        })
        handleSuccess()
      },
      onError: (err) => {
        toast.error(err.message)
      },
    })
  }

  return (
    <>
      <RouteDrawer.Body>
        <ExportFilters />
      </RouteDrawer.Body>
      <RouteDrawer.Footer>
        <div className="flex items-center gap-x-2">
          <RouteDrawer.Close asChild>
            <Button size="small" variant="secondary">
              {t("actions.cancel")}
            </Button>
          </RouteDrawer.Close>
          <Button onClick={handleExportRequest} size="small">
            {t("actions.export")}
          </Button>
        </div>
      </RouteDrawer.Footer>
    </>
  )
}

import { exportOrdersWorkflow } from "@medusajs/core-flows"
import {
  AuthenticatedMedusaRequest,
  MedusaResponse,
} from "@medusajs/framework/http"
import { HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/framework/types"

/**
 * @since 2.12.3
 */
export const POST = async (
  req: AuthenticatedMedusaRequest<{}, HttpTypes.AdminOrderFilters>,
  res: MedusaResponse<HttpTypes.AdminExportOrderResponse>
) => {
  const selectFields = req.queryConfig.fields ?? []
  const input = { select: selectFields, filter: req.filterableFields }

  const { transaction } = await exportOrdersWorkflow(req.scope).run({
    input,
  })

  res.status(202).json({ transaction_id: transaction.transactionId })
}

# Review of PR #35 (customer CSV export, closes #17)

The PR adds a customer export drawer and hook that closely copy the existing order export. But nothing behind them exists yet, and nothing in the dashboard links to them, so a user can't export customers. Your four questions are answered first, then a few other problems, then the filled-in rubric.

I read everything from the PR's commit (`d2f647cb`) and from `origin/develop` without checking out the branch. I fetched the PR into a local ref, `refs/remotes/pr/35`, so I could read files at that commit. I didn't run a build or typecheck, so anything I say about compile errors comes from reading the code.

## Your questions

**1. Does `sdk.admin.customer.export` exist, and is there anything behind it?**
No to both.
- `packages/admin/dashboard/src/hooks/api/customers.tsx:273` calls `sdk.admin.customer.export(query)`.
- The `Customer` class in `packages/core/js-sdk/src/admin/customer.ts` has no `export` method. Its methods are `create`, `update`, `list`, `retrieve`, `delete`, `batchCustomerGroups` and the address methods. Orders and products do have one (`order.ts:780`, `product.ts:229`).
- There's no `packages/medusa/src/api/admin/customers/export/route.ts`, though orders and products both have an export route.
- There's no export workflow for customers in core-flows.
- So the call should fail typechecking, and the dashboard build would likely fail with it. The PR description does admit the SDK method is missing, which is good, but the backend route and workflow are missing as well.

**2. Can a user reach the export?**
No.
- **Route map:** the `/customers` block in `packages/admin/dashboard/src/dashboard-app/routes/get-route.map.tsx:751-775` only has `create` under the list. Orders register `path: "export"` at line 398 and products at line 53, but there's nothing similar for customers.
- **Lazy loading:** `routes/customers/customer-export/` has no `index.ts`. Order export has `export { OrderExport as Component } from "./order-export"`, which the route map's lazy import needs. So even with a route entry, it wouldn't load.
- **Button:** `routes/customers/customer-list/` never mentions export. Orders link to it at `order-list-table.tsx:55` and `configurable-order-list-table.tsx:18`.

**3. Tests and changeset?**
- **Tests:** none are added. The PR says "the hook follows the same pattern as useExportOrders which is already tested", but I couldn't find any spec or test in the dashboard that refers to `useExportOrders` or `OrderExport`.
- **Changeset:** none (no `.changeset/` file in the diff), and that checklist box is unchecked.
- **CI:** no checks ran on the branch, and the testing section doesn't describe any manual verification.

**4. Why is `vite.config.mts` in this PR, and does it belong?**
- `packages/admin/dashboard/vite.config.mts:22-24` adds `resolve.dedupe: ["react", "react-dom"]`. The PR says this fixes a blank screen in the local dev server.
- It has nothing to do with #17 and changes the build config for everyone, so it should be its own issue and PR.
- The formatting is also off: line 23 has 7 spaces of indentation and line 24 ends with a stray tab after `},`.
- Your own notes say your stash fixes the blank dashboard with missing vite globals, which is a different cause. It's worth a team conversation about which fix is actually needed.

## Other findings

5. **Translation keys are missing.**
   - `customer-export.tsx:14, 17, 35, 36, 50` use `customers.export.header`, `.description`, `.success.title` and `.success.description`.
   - None of these exist in `packages/admin/dashboard/src/i18n/translations/en.json`, where `customers.export` is undefined. `orders.export` does have them.
   - The UI would show raw key strings, and the admin i18n validation workflow may flag it.
6. **It's less complete than the order flow it copies.** Order export shows the active filters in the drawer body (`ExportFilters`). This PR replaces that with a plain description (`customer-export.tsx:48-51`), so the user can't see which filters will apply. That's minor, but #17 asks to match the existing flows.
7. **Barrel export is out of order** (`hooks/table/query/index.ts:17`). The new export is appended at the end of a list that's otherwise alphabetical.
   - The PR describes this as "was missing". In fact every current caller imports the hook straight from `use-customer-table-query`, so it's only needed for this new component.
   - The change itself is harmless.
8. **No newline at end of file** in `customer-export.tsx:67`.
9. **PR template is mostly unfilled.** The Examples block is still placeholder text, and all four checklist boxes are unchecked, including "verified the code works as intended locally".
10. **No AI log comment on #17.** The issue has 0 comments, so there's nothing for the AI transparency row to check yet.

What's good: the hook and drawer match the `useExportOrders` / `OrderExport` code almost line for line, so it fits the codebase's style. Naming is clear, the commit message and branch name follow the course format, and the description is honest about the SDK gap.

**About #17 itself:** the issue has no numbered acceptance criteria, user scenario or Out of Scope section, so I judged the PR against the summary and user story. That matters for your own D2 grade and for how the author's D4 correctness gets scored. Also, "scope: small" assumed there was a pattern to reuse. With no customer backend at all, this is closer to medium: route, workflow, SDK method, then the UI. It would help to add acceptance criteria and maybe re-size the issue before the author revises.

## Rubric

I swapped the template's em dashes in the criterion names for colons, since you asked for none.

The drawer also isn't registered in `get-route.map.tsx`, has no `index.ts` for lazy loading, and there's no Export button on the customer list. |

## Summary

Closes #30 

**What** — What changes are introduced in this PR?

Adds a time interval control to the sales overview panel on the admin dashboard home page. Panel defaults to "Last 7 days" on page load. 4 presets are offered (Last 7 days, 30 days, 3 months, and 12 months) and a custom date range. 

**Why** — Why are these changes relevant or necessary?  

Before this, the panel showed all-time totals only. Store managers preparing a monthly or quarterly review, or checking a suspected slow period, couldn't see how the store performed over a specific time frame without leaving the home page.

**How** — How have these changes been implemented?

API (packages/medusa):

1. The validator accepts optional ISO start_date and end_date. Without them the range is the last 7 days.
2.  It returns a 400 if the end is is longer than 12 months. The counts calendar months, plus a day of slack for time zones and daylight saving changes, and it bounds how many orders one request can load. 
4. The route filters orders on created_at (time of purchase) within the range. An end_date in the future is treated as "now", because the dashboard sends the end of the last day.
6. The response now includes start_date and end_date.
7. The range rules live in a small new file, date-range.ts

Types (packages/core/types): AdminGetSalesSummaryParams and AdminSalesSummary have the new fields, documented with TSDoc.

Dashboard (packages/admin/dashboard):

1. useSalesSummary(query) puts the range in the query key, so each period is cached separately. It uses keepPreviousData, so the panel doesn't flash a skeleton when you switch periods.
2. The panel has the interval dropdown. Custom range shows two date pickers. They block an end before the start, any future date, and more than 12 months between the two.
3. The presets are computed in local time, and the choice isn't saved between visits.
4.  en.json has the new strings, and the "all-time" and "yet" wording is updated. Other languages fall back to English.

**Testing** — How have these changes been tested, or how can the reviewer test the feature?

1. Backend unit tests: packages/medusa/src/api/admin/analytics/__tests__/date-range.spec.ts covers the default range, the 12-month cap (including leap years and time zone slack), clamping, and the validator.
2. Dashboard tests: date-range.spec.ts covers the presets and picker limits. sales-summary-section.spec.tsx covers the default period, each preset's request, and the custom pickers appearing.
3. Integration tests: integration-tests/http/__tests__/analytics/admin/sales-summary.spec.ts covers the default 7-day window, orders inside and outside a range (backdated via SQL), future end-date clamping, and the 400 cases (end before start, range over 12 months, invalid date).
4. Results: backend unit 45/45, dashboard 18/18, integration 16/16 (Postgres on port 5433). Typechecks for the analytics files are clean. I did not run the validate-http-types CI check locally.

:00.000Z

## Decision

Whether to add a 12 month cap on the data on the dashboard, or take in data from all past orders, no matter how long ago. I decided to cap it at 12 months.  It's cheap, it protects the endpoint, and the year preset already tops out at the cap. Raising or removing it later is a one-line change. The all-time loss is the main cost, and the issue doesn't ask for all-time.

--
## User Story
As a store manager, I want to filter the sales analytics overview by a selected time interval so that I can understand how my store is performing over different time periods without leaving the home page.

## User Scenario
A user opens the dashboard home page and sees the analytics summary defaulting to the past 7 days. They're preparing for a monthly business review, so they switch the interval to "Last 30 days." The revenue total, order count, and top products all update in place. Later, they want to investigate a suspected slow period, so they set a custom date range covering two specific weeks and confirm their suspicion before heading to Orders to dig deeper.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The analytics summary panel includes a time interval control defaulting to "Last 7 days" on every page load.
2. Preset options available: Last 7 days and Last 30 days
3. A custom date range picker is also available, allowing the merchant to specify an arbitrary start and end date.
4. Selecting any interval or confirming a custom range updates all metrics (revenue, order count, top products) without a full page reload.
5. The custom date picker prevents invalid selections: end date cannot precede start date; future dates are not selectable.
6. Order timestamps (time of purchase) are used as the basis for interval filtering across all metrics.
7. If no orders fall within the selected interval, each metric displays a zero state rather than an error or blank space.

## Out of Scope
- Comparing two intervals side-by-side (e.g. "This month vs last month").
- Saving or persisting a merchant's last-used interval across sessions.
- Interval filtering on any page other than the dashboard home page analytics panel.

## Open Questions
- Should the custom date range be bounded (e.g. no more than 12 months) to guard against slow queries on large stores?

+import {
+  DEFAULT_RANGE_DAYS,
+  getRequestedRange,
+  isRangeWithinLimit,
+  resolveDateRange,
+} from "../date-range"
+import { AdminGetSalesSummaryParams } from "../validators"
+
+const NOW = new Date("2026-10-07T15:30:00.000Z")
+const DAY_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000
+
+describe("getRequestedRange", () => {
+  it("defaults to the last 7 days when no dates are given", () => {
+    const { start, end } = getRequestedRange({}, NOW)
+
+    expect(end).toEqual(NOW)
+    expect(start).toEqual(new Date(NOW.getTime() - DEFAULT_RANGE_DAYS * DAY_MS))
+  })
+
+  it("ends now when only a start date is given", () => {
+    const start_date = new Date("2026-09-01T00:00:00.000Z")
+
+    expect(getRequestedRange({ start_date }, NOW)).toEqual({
+      start: start_date,
+      end: NOW,
+    })
+  })
+
+  it("starts 7 days before the end when only an end date is given", () => {
+    const end_date = new Date("2026-09-30T23:59:59.999Z")
+
+    const { start, end } = getRequestedRange({ end_date }, NOW)
+
+    expect(end).toEqual(end_date)
+    expect(start).toEqual(new Date(end_date.getTime() - 7 * DAY_MS))
+  })
+})
+
+describe("isRangeWithinLimit", () => {
+  const end = new Date("2026-10-07T23:59:59.999Z")
+
+  it("allows a range of exactly 12 months", () => {
+    expect(isRangeWithinLimit(new Date("2025-10-07T23:59:59.999Z"), end)).toBe(
+      true
+    )
+  })
+
+  it("allows a range that is a few hours over because of time zones", () => {
+    expect(isRangeWithinLimit(new Date("2025-10-07T10:00:00.000Z"), end)).toBe(
+      true
+    )
+  })
+
+  it("allows a full year that includes a leap day", () => {
+    expect(
+      isRangeWithinLimit(
+        new Date("2024-03-01T00:00:00.000Z"),
+        new Date("2025-02-28T23:59:59.999Z")
+      )
+    ).toBe(true)
+  })
+
+  it("rejects a range longer than 12 months", () => {
+    expect(isRangeWithinLimit(new Date("2025-09-01T00:00:00.000Z"), end)).toBe(
+      false
+    )
+  })
+})
+
+describe("resolveDateRange", () => {
+  it("keeps dates in the past as they are", () => {
+    const start_date = new Date("2026-09-01T00:00:00.000Z")
+    const end_date = new Date("2026-09-14T23:59:59.999Z")
+
+    expect(resolveDateRange({ start_date, end_date }, NOW)).toEqual({
+      start: start_date,
+      end: end_date,
+    })
+  })
+
+  it("treats an end date in the future as now", () => {
+    const start_date = new Date("2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z")
+    const end_date = new Date("2026-10-07T23:59:59.999Z")
+
+    expect(resolveDateRange({ start_date, end_date }, NOW).end).toEqual(NOW)
+  })
+})
+
+describe("AdminGetSalesSummaryParams", () => {
+  it("accepts an empty query", () => {
+    expect(AdminGetSalesSummaryParams.safeParse({}).success).toBe(true)
+  })
+
+  it("parses ISO dates into Date objects", () => {
+    const result = AdminGetSalesSummaryParams.parse({
+      start_date: "2026-09-01T00:00:00.000Z",
+      end_date: "2026-09-14T23:59:59.999Z",
+    })
+
+    expect(result.start_date).toEqual(new Date("2026-09-01T00:00:00.000Z"))
+    expect(result.end_date).toEqual(new Date("2026-09-14T23:59:59.999Z"))
+  })
+
+  it("rejects an end date before the start date", () => {
+    const result = AdminGetSalesSummaryParams.safeParse({
+      start_date: "2026-09-14T00:00:00.000Z",
+      end_date: "2026-09-01T00:00:00.000Z",
+    })
+
+    expect(result.success).toBe(false)
+    expect(result.error?.issues[0].message).toContain("end_date")
+  })
+
+  it("rejects a range longer than 12 months", () => {
+    const result = AdminGetSalesSummaryParams.safeParse({
+      start_date: "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
+      end_date: "2025-06-01T00:00:00.000Z",
+    })
+
+    expect(result.success).toBe(false)
+    expect(result.error?.issues[0].message).toContain("12 months")
+  })
+
+  it("rejects a start date more than 12 months ago when no end date is given", () => {
+    const result = AdminGetSalesSummaryParams.safeParse({
+      start_date: "2020-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
+    })
+
+    expect(result.success).toBe(false)
+  })
+
+  it("rejects dates that are not valid", () => {
+    expect(
+      AdminGetSalesSummaryParams.safeParse({ start_date: "not-a-date" }).success
+    ).toBe(false)
+  })
+})

+/**
+ * Date range rules for `GET /admin/analytics/sales-summary` (issue #30).
+ *
+ * Kept free of other imports so both the request validator and the route can
+ * use it without pulling in the order helpers.
+ */
+
+/**
+ * How many days the summary covers when the request names no dates. The
+ * dashboard shows "Last 7 days" on every page load, so the API defaults to the
+ * same window.
+ */
+export const DEFAULT_RANGE_DAYS = 7
+
+/**
+ * The longest range a request may cover, in calendar months. The route reads
+ * every order in the range, so this bounds how much work one request can ask
+ * for.
+ */
+export const MAX_RANGE_MONTHS = 12
+
+/**
+ * Extra time allowed on top of `MAX_RANGE_MONTHS`. Clients send local day
+ * boundaries converted to UTC, so a "last year" range can run a few hours past
+ * twelve calendar months once time zones and daylight saving changes are
+ * counted. A day of slack keeps those requests valid.
+ */
+const MAX_RANGE_GRACE_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000
+
+const DAY_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000
+
+export type SalesSummaryDateParams = {
+  start_date?: Date
+  end_date?: Date
+}
+
+/**
+ * The dates a request actually covers, before they are clamped to "now". A
+ * missing end date means "up to now", and a missing start date means
+ * `DEFAULT_RANGE_DAYS` before the end.
+ */
+export const getRequestedRange = (
+  params: SalesSummaryDateParams,
+  now: Date = new Date()
+): { start: Date; end: Date } => {
+  const end = params.end_date ?? now
+  const start =
+    params.start_date ?? new Date(end.getTime() - DEFAULT_RANGE_DAYS * DAY_MS)
+
+  return { start, end }
+}
+
+/**
+ * Returns whether the range is no longer than `MAX_RANGE_MONTHS` (plus the
+ * grace period). Months are counted on the calendar, so a leap year doesn't
+ * make a one year range too long.
+ */
+export const isRangeWithinLimit = (start: Date, end: Date): boolean => {
+  const earliestStart = new Date(end)
+  earliestStart.setUTCMonth(earliestStart.getUTCMonth() - MAX_RANGE_MONTHS)
+
+  return start.getTime() >= earliestStart.getTime() - MAX_RANGE_GRACE_MS
+}
+
+/**
+ * Works out the range the route should query. The end is clamped to now:
+ * orders can't be placed in the future, and clients send the end of the
+ * current local day, which is usually still ahead of the server clock.
+ */
+export const resolveDateRange = (
+  params: SalesSummaryDateParams,
+  now: Date = new Date()
+): { start: Date; end: Date } => {
+  const { start, end } = getRequestedRange(params, now)
+
+  return { start, end: end.getTime() > now.getTime() ? now : end }
+}

1:import {
2:  AuthenticatedMedusaRequest,
3:  MedusaResponse,
4:} from "@medusajs/framework/http"
5:import { HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/framework/types"
6:import { ContainerRegistrationKeys } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
7:import { resolveDateRange } from "../date-range"
8:import { AdminGetSalesSummaryParamsType } from "../validators"
9:import {
10:  addOrdersToSalesSummary,
11:  createSalesSummaryAccumulator,
12:  EXCLUDED_ORDER_STATUSES,
13:  finalizeSalesSummary,
14:  SALES_SUMMARY_ORDER_FIELDS,
15:  SalesSummaryOrder,
16:} from "../helpers"
17:
18:/**
19: * How many orders to load per database query. Orders are processed in
20: * batches so memory use stays flat no matter how many orders the store has.
21: */
22:const ORDER_BATCH_SIZE = 500
23:
24:/**
25: * GET /admin/analytics/sales-summary
26: *
27: * Returns the store's sales performance for the admin dashboard home page
28: * (issue #42): total revenue, number of orders, and the top three products by
29: * units sold.
30: *
31: * The summary covers orders placed between `start_date` and `end_date` (issue
32: * #30). Without them it covers the last 7 days. Ranges are limited to 12
33: * months; see `../date-range.ts` for the rules.
34: *
35: * Only paid, non-draft, non-canceled orders in the store's default currency
36: * are counted. See `../helpers.ts` for the exact rules.
37: *
38: * The figures are computed on every request (there is no server-side cache);
39: * the dashboard caches the response for a few minutes instead.
40: */
41:export const GET = async (
42:  req: AuthenticatedMedusaRequest<undefined, AdminGetSalesSummaryParamsType>,
43:  res: MedusaResponse<HttpTypes.AdminSalesSummaryResponse>
44:) => {
45:  const { start, end } = resolveDateRange(req.validatedQuery)
46:  const dates = {
47:    start_date: start.toISOString(),
48:    end_date: end.toISOString(),
49:  }
50:
51:  const query = req.scope.resolve(ContainerRegistrationKeys.QUERY)
52:
53:  // 1. Find the store's default currency. Revenue is reported in this
54:  //    currency only, because orders placed in other currencies can't be
55:  //    added together without exchange rates (which Medusa doesn't track).
56:  const {
57:    data: [store],
58:  } = await query.graph({
59:    entity: "store",
60:    fields: [
61:      "supported_currencies.currency_code",
62:      "supported_currencies.is_default",
63:    ],
64:    pagination: { take: 1 },
65:  })
66:
67:  const currencyCode =
68:    store?.supported_currencies?.find((currency) => currency?.is_default)
69:      ?.currency_code ?? null
70:
71:  const accumulator = createSalesSummaryAccumulator()
72:
73:  // Without a default currency there is nothing meaningful to report, so we
74:  // return the zero state rather than an error.
75:  if (!currencyCode) {
76:    return res.json({
77:      sales_summary: { ...finalizeSalesSummary(accumulator, null), ...dates },
78:    })
79:  }
80:
81:  // 2. Page through all candidate orders and add each batch to the running
82:  //    totals. The database filters out drafts, canceled orders, other
83:  //    currencies, and orders outside the date range up front so we load as
84:  //    few rows as possible. Payment status can't be filtered in the database
85:  //    (it's derived from the payment collections), so that check happens in
86:  //    `addOrdersToSalesSummary`.
87:  let skip = 0
88:
89:  while (true) {
90:    const { data: orders } = await query.graph({
91:      entity: "order",
92:      fields: SALES_SUMMARY_ORDER_FIELDS,
93:      filters: {
94:        is_draft_order: false,
95:        status: { $nin: EXCLUDED_ORDER_STATUSES },
96:        currency_code: currencyCode,
97:        // The order's creation time (time of purchase) decides which range
98:        // it belongs to.
99:        created_at: { $gte: start, $lte: end },
100:      },
101:      pagination: {
102:        skip,
103:        take: ORDER_BATCH_SIZE,
104:        // A stable sort order is required when paginating with skip/take,
105:        // otherwise rows could be repeated or skipped between pages.
106:        order: { id: "ASC" },
107:      },
108:    })
109:
110:    addOrdersToSalesSummary(
111:      accumulator,
112:      orders as unknown as SalesSummaryOrder[],
113:      currencyCode
114:    )
115:
116:    // A short page means we've reached the last batch.
117:    if (orders.length < ORDER_BATCH_SIZE) {
118:      break
119:    }
120:
121:    skip += ORDER_BATCH_SIZE
122:  }
123:
124:  // 3. Convert the running totals into the response shape (sorting and
125:  //    trimming the top products list).
126:  return res.json({
127:    sales_summary: {
128:      ...finalizeSalesSummary(accumulator, currencyCode),
129:      ...dates,
130:    },
131:  })
132:}
```

diff --git a/packages/admin/dashboard/src/routes/home/components/sales-summary-section/date-range.spec.ts b/packages/admin/dashboard/src/routes/home/components/sales-summary-section/date-range.spec.ts

--- /dev/null
+++ b/packages/admin/dashboard/src/routes/home/components/sales-summary-section/date-range.spec.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,78 @@
+import { addYears, differenceInCalendarDays, subDays } from "date-fns"
+import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest"
+
+import {
+  getEarliestStart,
+  getLatestEnd,
+  getPresetRange,
+  PRESET_INTERVALS,
+} from "./date-range"
+
+// A fixed "now" in the middle of a day, so tests don't depend on the clock.
+const NOW = new Date(2026, 9, 7, 15, 30)
+
+const daysCovered = (range: { start: Date; end: Date }) =>
+  differenceInCalendarDays(range.end, range.start) + 1
+
+describe("getPresetRange", () => {
+  it("covers whole days, ending at the end of today", () => {
+    for (const interval of PRESET_INTERVALS) {
+      const { start, end } = getPresetRange(interval, NOW)
+
+      expect(start.getHours()).toEqual(0)
+      expect(start.getMinutes()).toEqual(0)
+      expect(end.getFullYear()).toEqual(2026)
+      expect(end.getDate()).toEqual(7)
+      expect(end.getHours()).toEqual(23)
+      expect(end.getMinutes()).toEqual(59)
+    }
+  })
+
+  it("includes today in the last 7 and 30 days", () => {
+    expect(daysCovered(getPresetRange("week", NOW))).toEqual(7)
+    expect(daysCovered(getPresetRange("month", NOW))).toEqual(30)
+  })
+
+  it("covers 3 and 12 calendar months for the quarter and year", () => {
+    // 2026-07-08 to 2026-10-07 and 2025-10-08 to 2026-10-07.
+    expect(getPresetRange("quarter", NOW).start).toEqual(new Date(2026, 6, 8))
+    expect(getPresetRange("year", NOW).start).toEqual(new Date(2025, 9, 8))
+  })
+
+  it("keeps the year preset within the custom picker's earliest start", () => {
+    const { start, end } = getPresetRange("year", NOW)
+
+    expect(start.getTime()).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(
+      getEarliestStart(end).getTime()
+    )
+  })
+})
+
+describe("custom range limits", () => {
+  it("does not allow starting more than 12 months before the end", () => {
+    const end = new Date(2026, 9, 7, 23, 59, 59, 999)
+
+    expect(getEarliestStart(end)).toEqual(new Date(2025, 9, 8))
+  })
+
+  it("does not allow ending in the future", () => {
+    const start = subDays(NOW, 3)
+
+    const latest = getLatestEnd(start, NOW)
+
+    expect(latest.getDate()).toEqual(7)
+    expect(latest.getHours()).toEqual(23)
+  })
+
+  it("does not allow ending more than 12 months after the start", () => {
+    const start = new Date(2024, 0, 15)
+
+    const latest = getLatestEnd(start, NOW)
+
+    // 2025-01-14 is the last day within 12 months of 2024-01-15.
+    expect(latest.getTime()).toBeLessThan(addYears(start, 1).getTime())
+    expect(latest.getFullYear()).toEqual(2025)
+    expect(latest.getMonth()).toEqual(0)
+    expect(latest.getDate()).toEqual(14)
+  })
+})
diff --git a/packages/admin/dashboard/src/routes/home/components/sales-summary-section/date-range.ts b/packages/admin/dashboard/src/routes/home/components/sales-summary-section/date-range.ts

--- /dev/null
+++ b/packages/admin/dashboard/src/routes/home/components/sales-summary-section/date-range.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,72 @@
+import {
+  addDays,
+  addYears,
+  endOfDay,
+  startOfDay,
+  subDays,
+  subMonths,
+  subYears,
+} from "date-fns"
+
+/**
+ * The time periods the sales overview can show (issue #30). `custom` lets the
+ * merchant pick the start and end dates themselves.
+ */
+export type SalesSummaryInterval =
+  | "week"
+  | "month"
+  | "quarter"
+  | "year"
+  | "custom"
+
+export const PRESET_INTERVALS = ["week", "month", "quarter", "year"] as const
+
+/**
+ * The period shown on every page load.
+ */
+export const DEFAULT_INTERVAL = "week" satisfies SalesSummaryInterval
+
+export type DateRange = {
+  start: Date
+  end: Date
+}
+
+/**
+ * Returns the date range for a preset, in the merchant's local time. Ranges
+ * are whole days and include today, e.g. "Last 7 days" is today and the six
+ * days before it. The backend rejects ranges longer than 12 months, so the
+ * year preset starts one day after the same date last year.
+ */
+export const getPresetRange = (
+  interval: (typeof PRESET_INTERVALS)[number],
+  now: Date = new Date()
+): DateRange => {
+  const today = startOfDay(now)
+
+  const start = {
+    week: subDays(today, 6),
+    month: subDays(today, 29),
+    quarter: addDays(subMonths(today, 3), 1),
+    year: addDays(subYears(today, 1), 1),
+  }[interval]
+
+  return { start, end: endOfDay(now) }
+}
+
+/**
+ * The earliest start date the custom picker allows for a given end date. It
+ * mirrors the backend's 12 month limit.
+ */
+export const getEarliestStart = (end: Date): Date =>
+  startOfDay(addDays(subYears(end, 1), 1))
+
+/**
+ * The latest end date the custom picker allows for a given start date: the
+ * end of today at the latest (future dates can't have orders), and no more
+ * than 12 months after the start.
+ */
+export const getLatestEnd = (start: Date, now: Date = new Date()): Date => {
+  const limit = endOfDay(subDays(addYears(start, 1), 1))
+
+  return limit < now ? limit : endOfDay(now)
+}

# Review of PR #49 (sales summary time interval, closes #30)

This is a strong PR. All seven acceptance criteria in #30 are met, it has unit, component and integration tests plus a changeset, and the date-range rules are cleanly separated on both sides. The main things to fix are the PR description and a few small gaps. The missing `created_at` index is real but older than this PR, and this PR actually reduces the load.

I read everything from the PR's commit (`98a7b52`) without checking out the branch. I fetched it into a local ref, `refs/remotes/pr/49`, the same way as before. I didn't run any tests myself.

## Acceptance criteria

| # | Criterion | Met? | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Defaults to "Last 7 days" on every load | Yes | `sales-summary-section.tsx:42-48` (state starts from `DEFAULT_INTERVAL` and isn't saved) and backend `date-range.ts:42-50` |
| 2 | Presets for 7 and 30 days | Yes, plus 3 and 12 months | `routes/home/.../date-range.ts` `getPresetRange`. The extra two match what the team agreed in the #30 comments. |
| 3 | Custom date range picker | Yes | `sales-summary-section.tsx:131-155` |
| 4 | All metrics update without reload | Yes | `hooks/api/analytics.tsx:52` puts the range in the query key, and `:54` keeps the previous numbers on screen while loading |
| 5 | End can't precede start, no future dates | Yes, in the picker and on the server | Picker min/max at `sales-summary-section.tsx:137-138` and `:149-150`. The server returns a 400 from `validators.ts:23` and clamps future end dates to now at `date-range.ts:76`. |
| 7 | Zero state when no orders | Yes | Existing empty states use the updated strings (`sales-summary-section.tsx:207, 214, 225`), and the integration tests check zero totals for out-of-range orders |

Criterion 6 is about which timestamp is used, so it's covered in the next section.

## Which timestamp and which orders

- **Timestamp:** it filters on order `created_at` (`sales-summary/route.ts:99`), as you expected.
- **Drafts:** excluded twice, by `is_draft_order: false` (`route.ts:94`) and by `status: { $nin: EXCLUDED_ORDER_STATUSES }` (`route.ts:95`). That list is `[DRAFT, CANCELED]` (`helpers.ts:26-29`).
- **Canceled:** excluded by the same status filter, and there's an integration test for it.
- **Deleted:** there's no explicit filter. It relies on `query.graph` leaving out soft-deleted rows by default. I believe that default holds, but no test covers a deleted order. One test would make it explicit.
- **Converted draft orders:** this one is worth checking. A draft order that's later converted keeps its original `created_at`, so its sale would land on the day the draft was created, not the day it was placed. That's a small mismatch with "time of purchase" in criterion 6. At minimum it's worth a test or a note in the description.

## Tests and changeset

**Changeset:** present. `.changeset/sales-summary-time-interval.md` marks medusa, types and dashboard as patch.

**Tests:** there are three layers, and they cover the criteria well.
- **Backend unit tests** (`packages/medusa/.../__tests__/date-range.spec.ts`): the default range, the 12-month cap including leap years and time-zone slack, clamping, and the validator's 400 cases.
- **Dashboard tests** (`date-range.spec.ts`, `sales-summary-section.spec.tsx`): the default, each preset's request, and the custom pickers appearing.
- **Integration tests** (`integration-tests/http/.../sales-summary.spec.ts:214-340`): backdated orders inside and outside the range, future end dates, and the 400s.

**Gaps:**
- **Criterion 5 in the UI:** the min/max helpers are tested, but nothing checks that the pickers actually pass them in (`sales-summary-section.tsx:137-150`).
- **Changing a custom date:** no test checks that editing a date sends a new request. The custom test only checks that the pickers appear.
- **Edge cases:** no tests for a soft-deleted order or a converted draft order.

**CI:** no checks ran on the branch. The description does document local results (45/45 backend, 18/18 dashboard, 16/16 integration). It also says the validate-http-types check wasn't run, which is honest.

## Performance

- **You're right about the index.** The order model's index list (`packages/modules/order/src/models/order.ts:137-198`) has `display_id`, `currency_code`, `is_draft_order` and others, but nothing on `created_at`. I also didn't find one in the order migrations. So `route.ts:99` can't use an index for the date range. Postgres will either scan the whole table or go through `currency_code` / `is_draft_order` and filter, and both of those columns match most rows.
- **This PR makes things better, not worse.** Before it, the endpoint loaded every order ever placed. Now it loads only orders in the range, and the 12-month cap limits that. The expensive part is loading items and payments for each order, and that shrinks a lot.
- **Paging adds work.** The loop pages with `skip`/`take` ordered by `id` (`route.ts:101-107`), so every 500 orders repeats the filtered query with a bigger offset. Without an index, each of those repeats is another scan.
- **Suggested fix:** an index on `order(created_at) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`, or a combined `(currency_code, created_at)` index, plus a migration. That touches the order module, so I'd file it as a small follow-up issue rather than block this PR.

## Other findings

1. **Future start date with no end date.** `?start_date=<tomorrow>` gets a 200 with zero totals instead of a 400.
   - Neither refine catches it (`validators.ts:23-37`), and `resolveDateRange` then produces a start that's after the end (`date-range.ts:42-50, 76`).
   - The dashboard can't send this, so it's minor, but a one-line refine would make the API consistent.
2. **The range goes stale if the tab stays open.** The preset range is computed once and kept in state (`sales-summary-section.tsx:46-48`). If the dashboard is left open past midnight, "Last 7 days" keeps showing the old window until the user picks the preset again. That's fine for this sprint, but worth knowing.
3. **No loading cue when switching periods.** Because of `keepPreviousData` (`hooks/api/analytics.tsx:54`), `isPending` stays false while a new range loads (`sales-summary-section.tsx:50, 83`). The old numbers show with no sign they're about to change. Dimming the panel while `isPlaceholderData` is true would fix that.
4. **Naming nit:** `setInterval` (`sales-summary-section.tsx:42`) shadows the global `setInterval`. Something like `setSelectedInterval` avoids the confusion.
5. **The PR description is a bit garbled in places:**
   - "the end is is longer than 12 months" doesn't make sense.
   - The How list jumps 1, 2, 4, 6, 7.
   - The examples are cut off ("cannot be longe", "toISOStr", a date split across two lines) and aren't in a code block.
   - The template's "Example usage" placeholder is still there.
   - The checklist lost its `[ ]` boxes, so you can't tell what's been done.
6. **Commit message:** the single commit is "base code and tests" (`98a7b52`). That doesn't follow the course's `feat: ... (#30)` format.
7. **Issue housekeeping:**
   - Criterion 2 in #30 still says only 7 and 30 days. Updating it to match the four presets you all agreed on would keep the spec and PR in sync.
   - #30 isn't on the Sprint 1 milestone, even though the instructor asked for it in the issue comments.
8. **AI transparency:** #30 has no AI log comment, and `ai-logs/sprint1/` has nothing for the PR author yet.

What's good:
- **Shared rules:** the backend `date-range.ts` holds the range logic, so the validator and the route use the same code.
- **Comments:** they explain why (the time-zone grace period, clamping the end to now, why `created_at`), not just what.
- **Types:** the HTTP types have TSDoc and stay in sync with the validator.
- **Translations:** the `$schema.json` update keeps the i18n check happy.
- **Design decision:** the 12-month cap is documented with alternatives and tradeoffs, and it lines up with the open question in #30.

### Suggestions

- Add a refine so a `start_date` in the future with no `end_date` returns a 400 instead of an empty 200 (`validators.ts:23-37`, `date-range.ts:42-50`).
- Check how converted draft orders should be counted. They keep the draft's `created_at`, so the sale lands on the day the draft was made (`route.ts:99`). A test or a note in the description would settle it.
- Add a test for a soft-deleted order. It's excluded today by the `query.graph` default, but nothing checks that.
- Add a component test that the pickers get their min/max limits (`sales-summary-section.tsx:137-150`) and one that changing a custom date sends a new request.
- Show a loading cue while switching periods, for example dimming the panel when `isPlaceholderData` is true (`hooks/api/analytics.tsx:54`, `sales-summary-section.tsx:50`).
- Rename `setInterval` to something like `setSelectedInterval` so it doesn't shadow the global (`sales-summary-section.tsx:42`).

The route pages with `skip`/`take` (`route.ts:101-107`), so each batch repeats the date filter without an index. This PR already reduces the load by narrowing the range, so it doesn't need to block.
- Clean up the PR description: "the end is is longer than 12 months", the How list numbering (1, 2, 4, 6, 7), the cut off examples ("longe", "toISOStr"), the leftover "Example usage" placeholder, and the missing checklist boxes.
